questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: For x > 2, the indefinite integral ∫ dx / ((x − 2)√(x² − 4)) is (c is an arbitrary constant)
questions.explanation: Put x − 2 = 1/t, so dx = −dt/t² and t > 0. Then x + 2 = 4 + 1/t = (4t + 1)/t and x² − 4 = (x − 2)(x + 2) = (4t + 1)/t², so √(x² − 4) = √(4t + 1)/t. The integrand becomes (−dt/t²) ÷ [(1/t) × √(4t + 1)/t] = −dt/√(4t + 1), and ∫ −dt/√(4t + 1) = −(1/2)√(4t + 1) + c. Since 4t + 1 = 4/(x − 2) + 1 = (x + 2)/(x − 2), the integral is −(1/2)√((x + 2)/(x − 2)) + c. (Check: differentiating gives 1/((x − 2)√(x² − 4)).) Forgetting the minus sign from dx = −dt/t² gives the positive answer; dividing by 1/2 instead of multiplying gives the factor −2; turning the fraction under the root upside down gives √((x − 2)/(x + 2)).
